subject.title: Dreaming needs configurable session/cron exclusions; isolated cron transcripts still enter session corpus

question: Should memory-core expose a supported Dreaming session-ingestion policy, and should that contract be a narrow typed source control or the broader per-agent, session-prefix, cron-ID, and regex filter proposed here?
rationale: The remaining work changes which persisted conversations may influence durable memory and adds compatibility-sensitive plugin configuration; source inspection cannot determine the intended permanent operator contract.

options.title: Add narrow typed policy
options.body: Expose a small policy for disabling session ingestion or excluding provenance-backed source classes such as runtime and cron automation.

options.title: Add broad filter block
options.body: Support agent IDs, session prefixes, cron IDs, and source regexes, accepting a larger long-term compatibility and support surface.

options.title: Keep automatic filtering only
options.body: Continue fixing known provenance and classification defects without supporting operator-defined exclusions.

recommendation.title: Add narrow typed policy
recommendation.body: Expose a small policy for disabling session ingestion or excluding provenance-backed source classes such as runtime and cron automation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product and compatibility decision about the permanent Dreaming configuration contract, and recent adjacent runtime history plus the issue timeline make this the strongest available routing candidate.
